content.value_statement: SwiftUI teams need consistent Liquid Glass adoption across new and existing screens. This skill provides focused guidance for native APIs, fallbacks, performance, and design review.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use glassEffect, GlassEffectContainer, glass button styles, and glassEffectID.
Reviews modifier order, shape consistency, interactivity, and iOS availability handling.
Suggests Liquid Glass refactors for surfaces, chips, buttons, cards, and grouped elements.
Provides SwiftUI snippet patterns for basic glass, grouped effects, and prominent buttons.
Points users to Apple documentation for current Liquid Glass API details.
limitations: It does not compile, run, or test SwiftUI projects by itself.
It depends on iOS 26+ APIs, so older systems need fallback UI.
It cannot verify private Apple API changes without current documentation.
It provides guidance, not a complete app design system.

use_cases.title: Add Liquid Glass to a Feature
use_cases.description: Plan surfaces, controls, shapes, interactivity, and fallback UI before changing SwiftUI views.

use_cases.title: Review a SwiftUI Pull Request
use_cases.description: Check availability guards, containers, modifier order, transitions, and consistent glass behavior.

use_cases.title: Plan Design System Adoption
use_cases.description: Define where Liquid Glass belongs across buttons, chips, cards, and grouped controls.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Glass
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one view or component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the swiftui-liquid-glass skill to add Liquid Glass to this SwiftUI component. Include iOS availability handling and a simple fallback.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Existing Components
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a small feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the swiftui-liquid-glass skill to refactor these SwiftUI controls with native Liquid Glass APIs. Explain container placement and interaction choices.

prompt_templates.title: Review Liquid Glass Usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the swiftui-liquid-glass skill to review this implementation for availability, modifier order, shape consistency, interactivity, and performance.

prompt_templates.title: Design Advanced Transitions
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for animated hierarchy changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the swiftui-liquid-glass skill to design morphing Liquid Glass transitions for this changing SwiftUI hierarchy. Include identifiers and animation guidance.

output_examples.input: Review a toolbar with several glass buttons.
output: Group related buttons in a GlassEffectContainer so effects render consistently.
Use prominent glass only for the primary action.
Keep interactive glass limited to controls that receive touch or pointer input.

output_examples.input: Plan a fallback for iOS 25 and earlier.
output: Use conditional availability around Liquid Glass-only APIs.
Provide a non-glass material or background for older systems.
Keep spacing and shapes similar so the fallback layout remains stable.

output_examples.input: Improve a card list with Liquid Glass.
output_examples.output: The response identifies candidate surfaces, recommends consistent rounded shapes, and warns against applying glass to every list item.

best_practices: Use native Liquid Glass APIs before custom blur implementations.
Apply glass effects after layout and appearance modifiers.
Use interactive glass only for controls that respond to user input.
anti_patterns: Applying glass to every surface without hierarchy or purpose.
Using interactive glass on static labels or decorative elements.
Omitting non-glass fallback UI for pre-iOS 26 users.

faq.question: Does this skill write SwiftUI code?
faq.answer: It can guide code generation and review, but the AI tool writes changes in your project.

faq.question: Which platforms does it target?
faq.answer: It focuses on SwiftUI apps using iOS 26+ Liquid Glass APIs.

faq.question: Can it replace Apple documentation?
faq.answer: No. It recommends Apple documentation for the most current API details.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No. The skill content is local guidance and reference material.

faq.question: Can it review existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks availability, containers, modifier order, interactivity, transitions, and design consistency.

faq.question: Does it support older iOS versions?
faq.answer: It recommends fallback UI for earlier versions, but Liquid Glass itself needs iOS 26+.
